world.title: Fighting rages in Yemen’s Taiz as UN warns nearly 260,000 displaced
world.summary: Fighting has escalated in Yemen's Taiz province, with government forces conducting numerous strikes against Houthi positions. The United Nations has issued a warning regarding the humanitarian crisis, indicating that nearly 260,000 people have been displaced due to the ongoing conflict. The situation remains critical as both sides continue to engage in violent confrontations, affecting civilian populations significantly.

world.title: Indian Family In Australia Considers Returning To India After Racist Threats In Brisbane, Accused Arrested
world.summary: An Indian-Australian family in Brisbane is contemplating returning to India due to safety concerns following alleged racist threats. The family feels frightened after a 19-year-old man, Harley Adams, was charged in connection with the incident at their apartment complex. They are considering ending their lease as a result of the distressing experience and ongoing fears for their safety.

world.title: Iran claims 7 oil tankers damaged in Hormuz, warns strikes on bases if US facilitates passage
world.summary: Iranian state television reported that seven oil tankers were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz, either by strikes or naval mines. This incident, if confirmed, could represent the largest number of vessels damaged in a single day since the Iran war began. Iran warned that it would target bases if the US facilitates passage through the waterway.

business.title: HPCL consolidated net profit falls 6% YoY to Rs 3,625 crore in Q2FY27
business.summary: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) reported a 6% decline in consolidated net profit for Q2 FY27, totaling Rs 3,625 crore. For the first half of FY27, the company faced a loss of Rs 8,639.45 crore, contrasting with a profit of Rs 7,970 crore in the same period of FY26, attributed to rising crude oil prices amid the West Asia conflict.

business.title: 1 bond verdict while investing in Yes Bank: Sources
business.summary: Yes Bank is formalizing legal action regarding its AT-1 bonds issue, following a Supreme Court verdict. Sources indicate that despite potential financial implications from the ruling, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation's commitment to Yes Bank remains strong. The bank is navigating the complexities of the prolonged litigation, which has been anticipated by the financial conglomerate.

business.title: Ultraviolette X-47 Venom Launched in India at Rs. 2.65 Lakh
business.summary: Ultraviolette has launched the X-47 Venom motorcycle in India at an introductory price of Rs. 2.65 lakh (ex-showroom). It is the first model to feature the new VX-100 100V architecture, equipped with an 11kWh battery pack that offers a claimed range of 343 km and a top speed of 155 km/h, marking a significant advancement in electric motorcycles.

technology.title: Casio’s new stainless-steel G-Shock uses magnets to protect its hands from hard knocks
technology.summary: Casio has launched the G-Shock GMC-2500 series, featuring an analog design inspired by the 1983 DW-5000C. The series includes stainless-steel models GMC-2500D-1A and GMC-2500D-1A2, along with resin-band options GMC-2500-1A, GMC-2500-1A8, and the gold GMC-2500G-9A. The watches incorporate magnets to protect the hands from impacts, enhancing durability for users.

technology.title: Nasa fires Moon rocket engine at full power in test for future Artemis missions
technology.summary: NASA conducted a significant test of an RS-25 rocket engine at Stennis Space Center, firing it for 500 seconds at 111% power. This test is part of preparations for future Artemis missions to the Moon. The engine's performance is crucial for ensuring the reliability and efficiency of the propulsion systems needed for upcoming lunar exploration efforts.

technology.title: Can a customer buy more than two iPhones at one time: Here’s what Apple Store 'warning' in India says
technology.summary: Apple has launched the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo in India. Customers looking to purchase multiple devices for family or gifts should note that Apple has implemented a limit on the number of iPhones that can be bought at one time. This policy aims to manage demand during the festive season.

sports.title: Aliss Al Islam reported for suspect bowling action
sports.summary: Bangladesh off-spinner Aliss Al Islam has been reported for a suspect bowling action during a tri-series match against Afghanistan, as announced by the International Cricket Council on October 22. The report follows scrutiny of his bowling technique during the match held in the United Arab Emirates. Further assessments will determine the validity of the concerns raised.

sports.title: Aliss Al Islam reported for suspect bowling action
sports.summary: Bangladesh off-spinner Aliss Al Islam has been reported for a suspect bowling action during the UAE Tri-Series match against Afghanistan. The International Cricket Council announced the report on October 22. Al Islam, known for his mystery spin, will undergo an assessment to determine if his bowling action complies with the regulations set by the governing body.

sports.title: Harry Brook goes berserk in Rawalpindi, breaks Shubman Gill's record for fastest ODI double century as England post 429/4
sports.summary: Harry Brook set a new record for the fastest double century in One Day Internationals (ODIs) during a match in Rawalpindi, surpassing Shubman Gill's previous record. Brook's explosive innings contributed to England's total of 429 runs for four wickets. The match highlighted Rawalpindi's reputation for speed and pace in cricket, showcasing Brook's remarkable batting performance.

health.title: Danish researchers confirm Guinea-Bissau vaccine seizure
health.summary: Danish researchers confirmed that police searched their premises in Guinea-Bissau as part of a controversial US-funded hepatitis B vaccine trial. The Bandim Health Project, involved in the trial, acknowledged the police action on Thursday. The search is linked to concerns regarding the vaccine's administration and the trial's ethical implications, raising questions about the research practices in the region.

health.title: Changes in breast shape and skin to swelling in armpits: Experts share the lesser-known symptoms of breast cancer beyond the lump
health.summary: Breast cancer symptoms extend beyond the common lump, according to experts. Lesser-known signs include changes in breast shape, skin texture, and swelling in the armpits. While about 90 percent of breast lumps are non-cancerous, awareness of these additional symptoms is crucial for early detection. Recognizing these signs can lead to timely medical intervention and potentially improve outcomes.

health.title: France reports first human Shamonda virus case, says no health risk
health.summary: France has reported its first human case of the Shamonda virus in an immunocompromised patient, who died earlier this month. Health authorities confirmed the virus, typically affecting livestock, was detected in this individual. Despite the case, officials stated there is no identified public health risk to the general population. Monitoring and assessments will continue as necessary.

science.title: Forget the Moon's south pole: 4 Other lunar sites could help astronauts build a base and prepare for Mars, new report reveals
science.summary: A new report highlights four lunar sites, aside from the Moon's south pole, that could provide insights into its ancient history and enhance scientific research. These locations are considered valuable for future astronaut missions to Mars, offering opportunities to build a base and prepare for interplanetary exploration. The findings aim to broaden the scope of lunar exploration.

science.title: NASA to hold Artemis press conference at Kennedy Space Center
science.summary: NASA will hold a press conference on October 23, 2026, at 2 p.m. EDT at Kennedy Space Center to provide updates on its Artemis moon missions. The event will feature insights from Jared Isaacman and other officials, focusing on Artemis III and related developments. This conference aims to inform the public about the progress and future plans for lunar exploration.

science.title: 3, Location, Latest News
science.summary: Centaurus X-3 is recognized as one of the brightest X-ray pulsars located in the constellation Centaurus. Recent scientific findings highlight its significance in astronomical studies. Researchers continue to explore its properties and implications for understanding pulsars and their behavior in the universe. Further updates and detailed information about Centaurus X-3 can be found in the latest news articles.

entertainment.title: Woman sends legal notice to actor Balu Varghese over alleged sexual misbehaviour
entertainment.summary: A woman has issued a legal notice to actor Balu Varghese, demanding a written undertaking and apology for alleged sexual misbehaviour during a private gathering. The notice outlines the incident, asserting it violates bodily autonomy, dignity, privacy, and personal security. The article also mentions two other women who have made similar allegations against the actor.

entertainment.title: Sanjay Leela Bhansali scolded Salman Khan for touching Aishwarya Rai,' recalls Smita Jayakar: 'He was in love but that wasn’t how the scene was supposed to be done'
entertainment.summary: Actor Smita Jayakar recalled an incident from the sets of Sanjay Leela Bhansali’s film ‘Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam’. She mentioned that Bhansali reprimanded Salman Khan for touching Aishwarya Rai Bachchan’s arm during the song ‘Aankhon Ki Gustakhiyan’. Jayakar noted that while Khan was in love, his actions did not align with the intended direction of the scene.
